title: Septic Arthritis Versus Transient Synovitis in Children
subject: Orthopedics
preview: Septic arthritis in a child is an urgent joint infection that may present with fever, severe pain and refusal to bear weight.
quickRevision: Septic arthritis in a child is an urgent joint infection that may present with fever, severe pain and refusal to bear weight.
Inflammatory markers, ultrasound and joint aspiration decisions require clinical context and specialist assessment.
Delay in septic arthritis diagnosis risks joint destruction and systemic infection.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Septic arthritis in a child is an urgent joint infection that may present with fever, severe pain and refusal to bear weight.
Transient synovitis may follow a viral illness and often has less systemic illness, but presentations overlap.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Inflammatory markers, ultrasound and joint aspiration decisions require clinical context and specialist assessment.
Delay in septic arthritis diagnosis risks joint destruction and systemic infection.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not rule out septic arthritis merely because a child has a recent viral history.

quiz.question: Which feature raises concern for septic arthritis over transient synovitis?
options: Well appearance with rapidly improving pain
Toxic appearance with inability to bear weight
quiz.explanation: Toxic appearance with inability to bear weight. Septic arthritis in a child is an urgent joint infection that may present with fever, severe pain and refusal to bear weight.
